title: code-review and PR scratchpad - cleanup + followups
body:
Quick context:
- PR #482: async kv-cache refactor + add partial cache invalidation endpoint (wip). Large diff, touches runtime cache layer, http handler, and a couple of unit tests that were flaky.
- Goal here: capture my review notes, checklist, and follow-ups so we don't lose items in GH comments.

High-level concerns:
- correctness: invalidation edge cases (concurrent requests + KV eviction) -> potential race between write-through and invalidate endpoint. See TODO #1 below.
- perf: new locking strategy reduces contention in common path but may add latency in cold-start path. Need microbench numbers.
- compatibility: ensure dedicated/dedicated-v2 config flags behave same. Missing a feature flag gate in handler.

Immediate checklist (for PR thread):
- [ ] Add integration test that simulates concurrent generate + invalidate (use harness INF-913 scenario).
- [ ] Add benchmark snippet: 95p latency and mean tokens/sec for sequence lengths 64/512 with vs without change.
- [ ] Add feature-flag gate: config.enable_partial_cache_invalidation (default off) + migration note.
- [ ] Add comment above InvalidateCacheHandler explaining eventual consistency guarantees (expected semantics).
- [ ] Update CHANGELOG with short note (breaking? no, opt-in) and include migration steps.
- [ ] Replace debug logs left in cache_manager.go: lines 213-218.

Code review nitpicks (smaller PR comments to leave):
- cache_manager.go: prefer ctx.Err() checks before non-blocking channel sends — safer for shutdown.
- invalidate_handler.go: too many nested ifs in handleReq -> extract validateRequest() helper.
- kv_client.go: exported function NewKVClient has nil-check but returns pointer; consider returning (Client, error) interface to mock easier.
- comments: >2 TODOs with GH links — either track in INF epic or resolve now.

Refactor ideas (follow-up PRs):
- 1) Split cache_manager into cache_core + cache_invalidation modules. Make core pure (no HTTP code) so it can be reused by edge-serving.
- 2) Introduce a lightweight in-memory metrics sampler (p95 rolling window) used by cache layer to adaptively set eviction threshold. Start as opt-in.
- 3) Replace custom lock with sharded mutex map to avoid hotspot on heavy concurrent token lookups. Evaluate with microbench.

Tests to add / stabilize:
- unit: ensure NewKVClient returns error for invalid configs (missing credentials).
- flaky test eyes: TestCacheEvictionConcurrent sometimes fails on CI (seen 3x in last 2 weeks) -> suspected race in test harness; mark as flaky and add retry + stronger assertions.
- integration: create stress test to generate thousands of short requests while triggering invalidation every ~200ms. Capture errors, latency distributions, and memory usage.

Follow-ups and owners (quick TODOs):
- TODO #1 (owner: Priya): "Investigate race when invalidate + write-through happen concurrently" -> add synchronized test using channel barriers. Target: 2026-02-26.
- TODO #2 (owner: Luca): "Add perf microbench + CI job" -> benchbinary + GitHub Actions job, use matrix for seq len 64/512/1024. Target: 2026-03-05.
- TODO #3 (owner: Samir): "Draft migration note + feature flag" -> small PR to product docs + changelog. Target: 2026-02-23.

Open questions (to discuss in async):
- Is partial invalidation semantics acceptable for Dedicated customers that pin model versions? Should invalidation be strictly synchronous for that tier? (product + SRE input needed)
- Should the invalidate endpoint be rate-limited at the proxy layer? If yes, how to expose telemetry to customers who rely on fast invalidations?
- Do we need a migration plan for customers using edge caches (partners)? Add to support playbook if yes.

Misc notes / scratch fragments:
- Could use existing prefix-cache TTL heuristics from edge-service. Pull logic into util/prefix_ttl.go?
- Remember to link GH PR to release notes board (release:v1.9).
- If we opt for sharded mutex, measure memory overhead vs throughput. Might be worth a feature-flagged implementation first.

Recent GH comments to copy into PR: 
- "+1 on helper extraction, makes handler much clearer" — Maya
- "Be careful with ctx usage; prefer context passed from http.Request" — Priya

Small patch ideas to unblock reviewers quickly:
- Add a short unit test that asserts invalidation sets a tombstone rather than immediate eviction (helps reason about consistency).
- Move one helper to a separate file to make diffs smaller (invalidate_util.go).

Last thought: prioritize safety over perf for initial rollout. Ship behind feature flag, gather perf metrics in Canary, then flip. Keep this doc updated with CI numbers and any flaky test markers.

End of scratchpad. Will trim and paste relevant items into GH comments + checklist before final review.
